text: A section of the M1 has reopened after a serious crash in Nottinghamshire.
A section of the M1 has been closed after a "serious" crash in Nottinghamshire.
Nottinghamshire Police: Nottinghamshire Police confirmed the northbound carriageway of the M1 was closed between junctions 25 and 26 following the incident just after 19:00 BST.
Following a vehicle fire and associated spillage that closed part of the road, a major motorway has reopened.
All trains to and from London Stansted Airport are currently cancelled because of an "unsafe" track defect.
On Thursday evening National Highways updated to say there were delays of 60 minutes on the M25 clockwise between junctions 29 and 31, with about six miles (9.6km) of congestion.
However National Highways warned there were still delays of about 60 minutes.
Anti-clockwise there were 90 minutes of delays between junction 4 and junction 1A with eight miles (12.8km) of congestion, it added.
But the delays were widespread, with eight-mile (12.8km) queues building up on the M25 clockwise.
National Highways said warned drivers there are still long delays in the area, and some lanes would close again from about 21:30 BST for further repairs overnight.
After about 40 minutes, firefighters appeared.
Essex Fire and Rescue Service: quick actions" of crews first on the scene "prevented the fire from spreading, protecting the block of flats nearby
Three fire crews and a surface rescue boat were sent to the scene via Ferry Lane at 03:32 and were stood down at 06:26 after helping pass four people into ambulance care.
Long delays were expected in the area, the highways body added.

Aberdeenshire councillor Geva Blackett has raised questions about the order in which crews were sent. It took nearly 50 minutes for firefighters to get to the scene from Tomintoul - about 24 miles (38km) away.
Police close off the motorway, with vehicles, signs and cones blocking the carriageway and directing a long stream of traffic on to a slip road
Six lanes of traffic on motorway have all been stopped with a police car parked in the centre. The cars are facing the camera and the image has been taken from  above the M25.
Queues of lorries and other vehicles travelling away from the camera on a motorway

The view from a traffic camera. Traffic is standstill and queued all the way along a motorway. There are three lanes and a slip road on the left hand side where the queues are, and on the right hand side there are also three lanes with traffic flowing.

A composite image from traffic cameras. Long queues of traffic on the right and the police closure on the left, with a series of vehicles, signs and red and white cones directing traffic off the motorway on to a slip road
